description: This course covers sequence alignment using BLAST and ClustalW; genome assembly with SPAdes and Velvet; gene prediction using GeneMark and Augustus; phylogenetic tree construction with MEGA and PHYLIP; protein structure prediction using AlphaFold; biological databases such as NCBI, Ensembl, and UniProt; data formats like FASTA, GenBank, and BAM; and data analysis using Python and R with Bioconductor. It also includes topics on next-generation sequencing technologies, variant calling with GATK, and RNA-seq analysis with tools like TopHat and Cufflinks.

clos.text: Define sequence alignment algorithms such as BLAST and ClustalW and their applications in genome and protein analysis.
Describe the structure and function of biological databases like NCBI, Ensembl, and UniProt and their role in bioinformatics research.
Explain the principles of genome assembly using tools such as SPAdes and Velvet and their impact on genomic studies.
Apply Python and R programming to analyze biological data using Bioconductor and perform statistical analysis of genomic datasets.
Evaluate the accuracy of phylogenetic trees constructed using MEGA and PHYLIP and interpret their biological significance.
